property.description:
Setting this option to Enabled improves HOCO accuracy significantly by using the subclock, but incurs certain restrictions.

The FLL function requires the subclock oscillator to be running and stabilized. When enabled and running the PLL or system clock from HOCO, the BSP will wait for both the Subclock Stabilization Time as well as the FLL Stabilization Time when setting up clocks at startup.

When FLL is enabled Software Standby and Deep Software Standby modes are not available.
Setting this option to Enabled will insert delays for clocking scaling and transitions to ensure voltage supply stability. See the RA8D1 HWM (R01UH0995EJ0100) section 8.11.1 for details.

The CPU clock (CPUCLK) is used as the operating clock of the CPU. \nMaximum frequency is 480MHz (For BGA 224 package)/400MHz (For LQFP 176 package).
The system clock (ICLK) is used as the operating clock of the DMAC, DTC, Flash, SRAM, Standby SRAM, System BUS, I/O ports and ICU. \nMaximum frequency is 240 MHz.

The Peripheral clock A (PCLKA) is used as the operating clock for the ETHERC, EDMAC, USBHS, SCI, I3C, CANFD, CNECC, SPI, CRC, DOC, ADC12, DAC12, RSIP-E51A, GPT, DOTF AES clock, CEU, MIPI, DRW, and LCDC bus. \nMaximum frequency is 120 MHz.

The Peripheral clock B (PCLKB) is used as the operating clock for the CAC, ELC, POEG, RTC, WDT, IWDT, AGT, ULPT, IIC, USBFS, SSIE, SDHI, TSN, ACMPHS, OSPI and DOTF bus clock. \nMaximum frequency is 60 MHz.
The Peripheral clock C (PCLKC) is used as the operating clock for the ADC12 module. \nMaximum frequency is 60 MHz.
The Peripheral clock D (PCLKD) is used as the operating clock for the GPT (count clock) module. \nMaximum frequency is 120 MHz.
The Peripheral clock E (PCLKE) is used as the operating clock for the CNECC (CANFD-RAM). \nMaximum frequency is 240 MHz.

The SDRAM clock (SDCLK) is an operating clock for the external bus controller.\nIt is output externally from the SDCLK pin for the SDRAM that is connected to the external bus. \nMaximum frequency is 120 MHz.
The external bus clock (BCLK) is an operating clock for the external bus controller.\nIt is also output externally from the BCLK pin for the external connection bus. \nMaximum frequency is 120 MHz.
Whether to output the BCLK frequency on the BCLKOUT pin. \nMaximum frequency is 60 MHz.

The flash-interface clock (FCLK) is used as the operating clock for the flash-memory interfaces.\nThat is, FCLK is used for programming and erasure of the ROM and E2 DataFlash, and reading from the E2 DataFlash. \nFrequency must be between 4 MHz and 60 MHz when any of these features are used.
Frequency output on the CLKOUT pin if CLKOUT is enabled. \nMaximum frequency is 60 MHz.
The SCI clock (SCICLK) is an operating clock for the SCI module. \nMaximum frequency is 120MHz.
The SPI clock (SPICLK) is an operating clock for the SPI module. \nMaximum frequency is 120MHz.
The CANFD clock (CANFDCLK) is an operating clock for the CANFD module. \nMaximum frequency is 80 MHz.
The LCD clock (LCDCLK) is an operating clock for the GLCD module. \nMaximum frequency is 240MHz.
The I3C clock (I3CCLK) is an operating clock for the I3C module. \nMaximum frequency is 200MHz.
The USB clock (UCK) is an operating clock for the USBFS/USBHS module.\nA 48-MHz clock must be supplied to the USB module.\nWhen the USB module is used, setting must be made so that UCK is 48 MHz.
The USB clock (U60CLK) is an operating clock for the USBHS module.\nA 60-MHz clock must be supplied to the USB module.\nWhen the USB module is used, setting must be made so that U60CLK is 60 MHz.
The Octal-SPI clock (OCTACLK) is an operating clock for the Octal-SPI module. \nMaximum frequency is 200MHz.
